correctness.rationale: Reconstructed section-2 contact Theta=(sum k J_k)/(sum k N_k) and demographic N_k prime=Lambda-mu N_k, hence at DFE N_k=S_k=Lambda/mu. Differentiating normalized Theta gives DTheta=(mu/(Lambda L)) sum k DJ_k, so the boundary incidence beta k S_k DTheta cancels Lambda/mu. With survival pi(a)=exp(-integral (mu+gamma+r)), infection inflows form a rank-one renewal operator whose positive-real growth characteristic equation is 1=beta (Q/L) int exp(-lambda a)pi(a) da. Under positive constant rates the age-integrated six-dimensional system closes exactly: independent symbolic differentiation of the nonlinear 6-vector at DFE (2,2,0,0,0,0) gives infected block [[-5/6,1/3],[1/3,-1/3]], eigenvalues -1 and -1/6, and all four other eigenvalues -1/2. Exact rational threshold Rcontact=5/6 versus printed Rsource=(Lambda/mu)5/6=5/3. The characteristic representation also bounds infection-age L1 via decaying boundary influx and positive survival loss >=mu+gamma, establishing local asymptotic stability of this constant-rate subfamily, not general PDE stability. No unproved sign from simulations is used.
residual_risks: The corrected general-age formula characterizes positive-real infection-invasion modes, not a complete global nonlinear spectral/stability theorem.
The explicit stability counterexample uses constant rates; no assertion is made about all recovery-age profiles or backward bifurcation analysis.
A different intentionally unnormalized contact model would have a different threshold, but it is not the literal Section 2 equations; an unindexed erratum could repair these formulas.

Other network epidemiology threshold papers use distinct models/contact normalization and do not supply this source-specific contradiction.

final_claim: For the literal normalized degree-half-edge contact probability and equal per-class recruitment of Yang–Martcheva–Zhang–Sun (2026), linearized invasion threshold is beta (sum k^2/sum k) integral survival, without Lambda/mu.
